title: Island Count After Each Land Addition
statement: You are given a grid with rows rows and cols columns that starts as all water. You are also given positions, a list of [r, c] pairs. Process the pairs in order; each one turns the cell at row r, column c into land. After processing each pair, record the current number of islands, where an island is a maximal group of land cells connected 4-directionally (up, down, left, right). Return the list of these recorded counts, one entry per pair in positions, in the same order. If a pair names a cell that is already land, the grid does not change and you still record the current (unchanged) count for that step. Recommended approach: flatten cell (r, c) to the id r*cols + c, keep a running island counter, increment it by one for every genuinely new land cell you create, and decrement it by one for each successful union with an already-land 4-directional neighbor (a union that actually merges two distinct components). If positions is empty, return an empty list.
hints: Each addition only ever connects the new cell to cells that already exist, so think about a structure that merges groups incrementally rather than rescanning the whole grid every step.

Maintain a disjoint-set forest over flattened cell ids plus a single running island counter: +1 when a brand-new land cell appears, and rely on your union routine's return value to know whether a neighbor merge actually reduced the count.

For each new cell: skip it entirely (and repeat the last count) if it is already land; otherwise add it, do count += 1, then for each of the four in-bounds land neighbors call union and only do count -= 1 when union reports that two distinct components were actually joined. A cell that touches two arms of the same existing island unions successfully only once, so the count drops by at most one for that cell.
